newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares end off peaks on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares end off peaks on profit-taking.

text.p: Profit-taking by speculators trimmed early gains as share prices closed marginally higher in mixed trade in Delhi on Tuesday, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index closed 1.50 points higher at 788.43 points. The index had surged to 793.99 in earlier afternoon trade.

Brokers said foreign institutional investors (FIIs) and speculators made heavy purchases in Smithkline Beecham Consumer Healthcare Ltd in the last 15 minutes of trading following its announcement of a bonus share issue.
Smithclime Beecham, which offered three shares for every five shares held, shot up 26 rupees, or 9.5 percent, to 300 rupees, fuelled by FII and speculative purchases, brokers said.

The company said in a statement that its after-tax profit jumped 30 percent to 469.4 million rupees for the financial year ended on December 31. Profit before tax was 793.1 million rupees, it added without giving a comparative figure for 1995.
"Most of the stocks could not consolidate their higher levels as profit-taking trimmed early gains," said Harish Malhotra of brokers Malhotra Financial Services.
Reliance Industries ended 4.15 rupees higher at 292.25 as marketmen continued to mop up its shares following news that a recent payment of tax by the company will not dent its profits significantly.
State Bank of India fell 2.0 rupees to 320.50 on profit-taking.
